observations: Two large circular forms dominate the center, filled with concentric yellow-gold rings that brighten toward white at their cores, set against a dark surrounding shape.
Diagonal rays of pale yellow-white spread from the lower corners outward, overlaying dense layered line work across the whole composition.

The border area carries competing line types: pink scalloped waves along the top, blue segmented shapes upper-right, red zigzags, and loose black scribbles, layered without a clear foreground-background order.
reading: Two glowing circular forms burn at the center, their concentric rings pulling the eye inward while pale rays push outward from the lower corners. The surrounding surface is packed with competing marks—zigzags, loops, dots, and segmented shapes in red, blue, teal, and gold. The effect reads less as decoration than as pressure: something close to overwhelm held just inside a frame.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #112 and nnxyz nnotb #114, both flat-field silhouette works with sparse marks. The density of layered line work here stands in strong contrast to those neighbors, showing the range the collector values.

connections.reason: Both works center a face-like arrangement of two large circular eye forms built from concentric rings, though nifty faces #68 uses dark spiraling rings on a cool teal ground while #113 uses bright gold rings with radiating pale rays.

lookingQuestion: Where does your eye settle first—on the bright cores of the two circular forms, or on the rays spreading outward from the lower corners—and what pulls it there?
ambiguities: The face-like reading of the central form is a viewer inference; the image shows circular and rectangular shapes but no labeled subject.
